context: A 2x2 small-multiples choropleth comparing four classification methods (Quantile, Equal Interval, Jenks, Manual Threshold) on synthetic US median household income data, with a shared slider to change class count (3-7), cross-map hover highlighting, and a shared histogram below showing all four methods' breakpoints overlaid.
first_impression: The 2x2 grid reads as a single comparison unit rather than four independent views, making the classification-difference lesson immediately legible.
what_works: Consistent sequential yellow-brown palette across all four panels keeps cognitive load low — the viewer compares state coloring differences without having to re-learn the encoding per panel. The histogram with four overlaid breakpoint lines is a smart analytical anchor that grounds the abstract classification differences in the actual data distribution.
what_doesnt: Legend labels under each map are rendered at 9px monospace with dollar-range strings — at panel size they are nearly unreadable and require zooming to parse. The histogram overlay of four dash-patterned breakpoint lines in four colors is dense: with up to 28 lines drawn simultaneously (7 classes × 4 methods), the lines stack heavily and the dash pattern distinctions become hard to track without careful study.
